subproblems.title: Push-forward of an integer multiplicity current by a linear isometric embedding is integer multiplicity and keeps its mass (parent steps 1–2)
subproblems.statement: Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P and Hᵈ = μHE[d] (Mathlib's normalized Euclidean Hausdorff measure). For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d (smooth d-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U) and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d; ∂X = X.boundary (∂X(ω) = X(dω), d = exteriorDerivative); X − Y is the contract subtraction (pointwise on test forms). For G ⊆ ℝ^P, M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of max(X(ω), 0) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, where |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors (covectorEuclideanNorm: |α|² = Σ_I α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(d−1)})² over strictly increasing I); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in U is the contract structure IMRep U d; R represents X when X(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHᵈ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U), where ⟨ω, ξ⟩(x) = ξ(x)(ω(x)); μ_R = θ·Hᵈ⌞M is R.measure; X is integer multiplicity (IM, IsIntegerMultiplicity X) if some IMRep represents it. e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 denotes the standard basis vector of the respective space; castSucc : Fin P → Fin (P + 1) and last = Fin.last P. Let P, Q, d ∈ ℕ, let L : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be a continuous linear map which is an isometry (|Lx − Lx'| = |x − x'|), let hL be a proof that x ↦ 0 + Lx is a proper map (automatic for an isometry; it is only needed to form the push-forward), and let T ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (domain univ) be integer multiplicity. Let L#T := GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward L 0 hL T ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^Q) (domain univ = preimage of univ; Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 for the proper linear map L), i.e. L#T(ω) = T(L^#ω) with L^#ω(x) = ω(Lx)(L·, …, L·). Then L#T is integer multiplicity and M(L#T) = M(T) in [0, ∞].

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–2 of the parent-supplied proof (the push-forward ι₀#T of T by the embedding ι₀ : ℝ^P → ℝ^{P+1} is IM, and by (C1) M(ι₀#T) = μ(ι₀(M)) = M(T)), i.e. Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 and 3.3–3.9 for a linear isometric embedding, whose Jacobian is 1; here for an arbitrary linear isometry L : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q. Tools: (C1) = the accepted declaration dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support (for open U, X ∈ 𝒟_d(U) and an IMRep R in U representing X, M_W(X) = μ_R(W) for every open W); Mathlib Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure (μHE[d].map f = μHE[d].restrict (range f) for an isometry f between metric spaces), Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, Isometry.isClosedEmbedding, Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding, MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map, MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map / lintegral_map / ae_map_iff / aestronglyMeasurable_map_iff; SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward_apply, affinePullbackTestOn, affinePullbackForm.
1. Facts about L. Since L is linear and isometric, ⟨Lx, Lx'⟩ = ⟨x, x'⟩ (polarization), so L is injective and has a continuous linear left inverse L⁺ (e.g. the adjoint L*: ⟨L*Lx, y⟩ = ⟨Lx, Ly⟩ = ⟨x, y⟩ for all y, so L*L = id). L is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding; ℝ^P is complete), hence a measurable embedding: L(A) is Borel for Borel A; and L⁻¹(K) is compact for compact K ⊆ ℝ^Q. For every A ⊆ ℝ^P, Hᵈ(L(A)) = Hᵈ(A) (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), and the measures satisfy (Hᵈ⌞A).map L = (Hᵈ.map L)⌞L(A) = (Hᵈ⌞range L)⌞L(A) = Hᵈ⌞L(A) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map together with L⁻¹(L(A)) = A by injectivity, Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, and Measure.restrict_restrict_of_subset since L(A) ⊆ range L; no measurability of A is needed). Consequently, for every A ⊆ ℝ^P and every g : ℝ^Q → ℝ, ∫_{L(A)} g dHᵈ = ∫_A g∘L dHᵈ (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map; no integrability hypothesis is needed, both sides being Bochner integrals), and likewise ∫⁻_{L(A)} g dHᵈ = ∫⁻_A g∘L dHᵈ for g : ℝ^Q → [0, ∞].
2. Covectors and multivectors. For a d-covector β on ℝ^Q let L^*β := β(L·, …, L·) = β.compContinuousLinearMap L; β ↦ L^*β is the continuous linear map ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMapCLM L. For ζ ∈ MultiVector P d (a continuous linear functional on d-covectors of ℝ^P) let (∧L)ζ := ζ ∘ L^* ∈ MultiVector Q d, i.e. (∧L)ζ(β) = ζ(L^*β); ∧L is continuous linear. By definition of affinePullbackForm with b = 0, L^#ω(x) = (ω(0 + Lx)).compContinuousLinearMap L = L^*(ω(Lx)).
3. Approximate tangent spaces are transported. Claim: if M ⊆ ℝ^P has approximate tangent space Q₀ at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d M x Q₀), then L(M) has approximate tangent space L(Q₀) := Q₀.map L at Lx. Proof: (i) dim L(Q₀) = dim Q₀ = d because L is injective. (ii) For r > 0 and w ∈ ℝ^P, blowUpMap (Lx) r (Lw) = r⁻¹(Lw − Lx) = L(r⁻¹(w − x)) = L(blowUpMap x r w), so blowUpMap (Lx) r '' L(M) = L(blowUpMap x r '' M). (iii) Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q). Then f∘L is continuous and tsupport(f∘L) ⊆ L⁻¹(tsupport f) is compact (step 1), so f∘L ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). By step 1 and (ii), ∫_{blowUpMap (Lx) r '' L(M)} f dHᵈ = ∫_{L(blowUpMap x r '' M)} f dHᵈ = ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' M} f∘L dHᵈ, which tends to ∫_{Q₀} f∘L dHᵈ as r ↓ 0 by the hypothesis applied to f∘L; and ∫_{Q₀} f∘L dHᵈ = ∫_{L(Q₀)} f dHᵈ by step 1, since (Q₀.map L : Set ℝ^Q) = L(Q₀). ∎
4. Unit orientations are transported. Claim: if IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q₀, i.e. ξ(α) = s·α(τ₁, …, τ_d) for all α, with s ∈ {1, −1} and τ orthonormal spanning Q₀, then IsUnitOrientationOf ((∧L)ξ) (L(Q₀)). Proof: (∧L)ξ(β) = ξ(L^*β) = s·(L^*β)(τ) = s·β(Lτ₁, …, Lτ_d) for every d-covector β of ℝ^Q; the family Lτ is orthonormal (L preserves inner products) and span(range(L∘τ)) = (span(range τ)).map L = L(Q₀). ∎
5. The image triple. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in ℝ^P (U = univ) representing T. Define R̃ with carrier L(M), multiplicity θ∘L⁺ and orientation (∧L)∘ξ∘L⁺; note θ(L⁺(Lx)) = θ(x) and (∧L)ξ(L⁺(Lx)) = (∧L)ξ(x). R̃ is an IMRep in ℝ^Q: (a) L(M) is Borel (step 1) and ⊆ univ. (b) Countable d-rectifiability: from M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^d) with Hᵈ(M₀) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz, L(M) ⊆ L(M₀) ∪ ⋃_j (L∘F_j)(ℝ^d), where Hᵈ(L(M₀)) = Hᵈ(M₀) = 0 and L∘F_j is Lipschitz. (c) θ∘L⁺ is measurable (L⁺ continuous) and θ(L⁺y) = θ(x) > 0 for y = Lx ∈ L(M). (d) Local integrability: for compact K ⊆ ℝ^Q, L(M) ∩ K = L(M ∩ L⁻¹(K)), so by step 1 ∫⁻_{L(M)∩K} θ∘L⁺ dHᵈ = ∫⁻_{M ∩ L⁻¹(K)} θ dHᵈ < ∞, because L⁻¹(K) is a compact subset of ℝ^P. (e) Measurability of the orientation: Hᵈ⌞L(M) = (Hᵈ⌞M).map L (step 1), and ((∧L)∘ξ∘L⁺)∘L = (∧L)∘ξ is Hᵈ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (ξ is, and ∧L is continuous linear); by MeasurableEmbedding.aestronglyMeasurable_map_iff the orientation of R̃ is Hᵈ⌞L(M)-a.e. strongly measurable. (f) Orientation of approximate tangent spaces: for Hᵈ⌞M-a.e. x there is Q₀ with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt d M x Q₀ and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q₀; by steps 3 and 4, L(Q₀) is an approximate tangent space of L(M) at Lx and is unit-oriented by (∧L)ξ(x) = (∧L)ξ(L⁺(Lx)). Since Hᵈ⌞L(M) = (Hᵈ⌞M).map L, MeasurableEmbedding.ae_map_iff turns this into the required statement for Hᵈ⌞L(M)-a.e. y.
6. R̃ represents L#T. For ω ∈ 𝒟ᵈ(ℝ^Q), L^#ω = affinePullbackTestOn L 0 hL univ d ω ∈ 𝒟ᵈ((x ↦ 0 + Lx)⁻¹(univ)) = 𝒟ᵈ(ℝ^P) (the domain (fun x => 0 + L x) ⁻¹' univ is definitionally univ, so one moves between the two with show/change rather than rw), and L#T(ω) = T(L^#ω) (affinePushforward_apply, a rfl lemma). As R represents T and by step 2, T(L^#ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(L^*(ω(Lx))) dHᵈ(x) = ∫_M θ(x) ((∧L)ξ(x))(ω(Lx)) dHᵈ(x) = ∫_M g(Lx) dHᵈ(x), where g(y) := θ(L⁺y)·((∧L)ξ(L⁺y))(ω(y)). By step 1 this equals ∫_{L(M)} g dHᵈ = R̃.action ω. Hence R̃ represents L#T, and L#T is IM.
7. Mass. R̃.measure(ℝ^Q) = ∫⁻_{L(M)} θ∘L⁺ dHᵈ = ∫⁻_M θ dHᵈ = R.measure(ℝ^P) by step 1 (IMRep.measure = (Hᵈ⌞carrier).withDensity mult). By (C1) with U = W = ℝ^P (open), M(T) = M_{ℝ^P}(T) = R.measure(ℝ^P); by (C1) with U = W = ℝ^Q and the IMRep R̃ of step 6, M(L#T) = R̃.measure(ℝ^Q). Hence M(L#T) = M(T) in [0, ∞]. ∎
proof_key_steps: Linear isometries: Hᵈ⌞L(A) = L_#(Hᵈ⌞A), so ∫_{L(A)} g dHᵈ = ∫_A g∘L dHᵈ; L is a proper measurable embedding with a continuous linear left inverse.
Approximate tangent spaces and unit orientations are transported: T_{Lx}L(M) = L(T_xM), oriented by (∧L)ξ(x) = ξ(x)∘L^*.
The image triple (L(M), θ∘L⁺, (∧L)ξ∘L⁺) is an IMRep in ℝ^Q representing L#T, by the change of variables applied to T(L^#ω).
Its measure of ℝ^Q equals μ_R(ℝ^P), so (C1) on both sides gives M(L#T) = M(T).

Tools: SimonGMT affinePullbackForm (with L = p, b = 0), affinePullbackForm_isSmoothForm, tsupport_affinePullbackForm_subset, exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm, iteratedFDeriv_affinePullbackForm and affinePullbackJet; Mathlib ContDiffBump (one_of_mem_closedBall, nonneg, le_one, tsupport_eq), tsupport_smul_subset_right, Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq, tsupport_iteratedFDeriv_subset, norm_iteratedFDeriv_smul_le (Leibniz bound), ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_coord_zero.
1. The cut-off and the operator. As K is compact it is bounded: K ⊆ B_r(0) for some r > 0. Let ζ : ℝ^{P+1} → ℝ be a C^∞ bump function (ContDiffBump centred at 0 with rIn = r + 1, rOut = r + 2): 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, ζ = 1 on the closed ball B̄_{r+1}(0), and tsupport ζ = B̄_{r+2}(0) is compact. Put V := B_{r+1}(0), an open set containing K, and E(ω) := ζ·p^#ω, i.e. E(ω)(y) := ζ(y)·(ω(py)).compContinuousLinearMap p = ζ(y)·affinePullbackForm p 0 ω (y) (note 0 + py = py).
2. E maps 𝒟ᵈ(ℝ^P) linearly into 𝒟ᵈ(ℝ^{P+1}). p^#ω is C^∞ (affinePullbackForm_isSmoothForm) and ζ is C^∞, so E(ω) is C^∞; tsupport E(ω) ⊆ tsupport ζ is compact, so E(ω) has compact support; tsupport E(ω) ⊆ univ trivially. E(ω + η) = E(ω) + E(η) and E(cω) = cE(ω) pointwise, because ω ↦ ω(py).compContinuousLinearMap p is linear. Property (i) holds because ζ = 1 on V.
3. Property (iii): tsupport(ζ·p^#ω) ⊆ tsupport(p^#ω) (tsupport_smul_subset_right) ⊆ (y ↦ 0 + py)⁻¹(tsupport ω) = p⁻¹(tsupport ω) (tsupport_affinePullbackForm_subset with L = p, b = 0, then zero_add).
4. Property (ii): let y ∈ V. V is open and ζ = 1 on V, so E(ω) and p^#ω agree on a neighbourhood of y; hence they have the same exterior derivative at y (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq; equivalently, the same Fréchet derivative by Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq, and exteriorDerivative f y = extDeriv f y = alternatizeUncurryFin (Df(y))). Since ω is smooth, exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm gives d(p^#ω) = p^#(dω), so (dE(ω))(y) = (dω)(0 + py).compContinuousLinearMap p = (dω)(py)(p·, …, p·).

Indeed p e_{castSucc i} = e_i for i ∈ Fin P and p e_last = 0 (by the defining formula of p, castSucc being injective and never equal to last). Let J : Fin d → Fin (P+1) be strictly increasing. If last ∈ range J, then (p^*α)(e_{J(0)}, …, e_{J(d−1)}) = α(p e_{J(0)}, …, p e_{J(d−1)}) has a zero argument, so it vanishes (map_coord_zero). Otherwise J = castSucc ∘ I for a unique I : Fin d → Fin P, which is strictly increasing because castSucc is an order embedding, and (p^*α)(e_J) = α(e_I). The map I ↦ castSucc ∘ I is a bijection from the strictly increasing I : Fin d → Fin P onto the strictly increasing J : Fin d → Fin (P+1) with last ∉ range J. Therefore |p^*α|² = Σ_J (p^*α)(e_J)² = Σ_I α(e_I)² = |α|². Next, |c·β| = |c|·|β| for c ∈ ℝ (the coefficients scale by c). Hence |E(ω)(y)| = |ζ(y)|·|p^*(ω(py))| = ζ(y)·|ω(py)| ≤ |ω(py)|, using 0 ≤ ζ(y) ≤ 1.
6. Property (v). Let ω_j → 0 in the sense of TestFormOnConverges: there is a compact C ⊆ ℝ^P with tsupport ω_j ⊆ C for all j, and for every k, D^kω_j → 0 uniformly on C. Since tsupport D^kω_j ⊆ tsupport ω_j ⊆ C (tsupport_iteratedFDeriv_subset), D^kω_j vanishes off C; hence ε_{j,k} := sup_{x ∈ ℝ^P} ‖D^kω_j(x)‖ → 0 as j → ∞, for every k (in a formalization it is convenient to use the equivalent form: for every ε > 0, eventually in j, ‖D^kω_j(x)‖ < ε for all x ∈ ℝ^P). By iteratedFDeriv_affinePullbackForm, D^l(p^#ω_j)(y) = A_l(D^lω_j(py)), where A_l = affinePullbackJet p d l is a fixed continuous linear map; so sup_y ‖D^l(p^#ω_j)(y)‖ ≤ ‖A_l‖·ε_{j,l}. Each D^iζ is continuous with compact support, hence Z_i := sup_y ‖D^iζ(y)‖ < ∞. By the Leibniz bound for a scalar function times a vector-valued function (norm_iteratedFDeriv_smul_le), for all y, ‖D^k(ζ·p^#ω_j)(y)‖ ≤ Σ_{l=0}^{k} C(k, l)·Z_{k−l}·‖A_l‖·ε_{j,l}, and the right-hand side tends to 0 as j → ∞. Thus for every k, D^kE(ω_j) → 0 = D^k(0) uniformly on ℝ^{P+1}, in particular on the compact set K' := tsupport ζ, which contains tsupport E(ω_j) for every j (step 2) and tsupport 0 = ∅, and K' ⊆ univ. This is TestFormOnConverges (j ↦ E(ω_j)) 0. ∎

Source: steps 5(c) and 9 of the parent-supplied proof (if P ∈ range ι_p one of the vectors is p(e_P) = 0 and the term vanishes; otherwise range ι_p = {0, …, P − 1}, p e_{ι_p(k)} = e_k, and p maps F̃_p isometrically onto the cube G_{z'}, so the two integrals agree; and G_{z'} = p(F̃_p)). Tools: Mathlib ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_coord_zero (via the alternating map ω(py)), Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure (μHE[N].map j = μHE[N].restrict (range j) for an isometry j : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N+1}), Isometry.isClosedEmbedding, Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding, MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map and MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map.
1. The images of the basis vectors. For j ∈ Fin (N+1) and i ∈ Fin N, (p e_j)_i = (e_j)_{castSucc i}, which is 1 if j = castSucc i and 0 otherwise. Hence p e_{castSucc k} = e_k for k ∈ Fin N, and p e_last = 0 because castSucc i ≠ last for all i.
2. Part (a). Let ι(k₀) = last. Then the k₀-th argument of the tuple (pe_{ι(0)}, …, pe_{ι(N−1)}) is p e_last = 0 (step 1), so for every y the multilinear map ω(py) vanishes on this tuple (map_coord_zero). The integrand is the zero function on ℝ^{N+1}, and the integral is 0.
3. Part (b), ι = castSucc. Assume last ∉ range ι. If N = 0, then ι = castSucc trivially (both are the empty map Fin 0 → Fin 1); F̃ is then the single point with last coordinate ρz_last, G = ℝ⁰ is a point, and steps 4–5 below apply unchanged. For N ≥ 1, a strictly increasing ι : Fin N → Fin (N+1) satisfies ι(k) ≥ k (induction on k). Moreover ι(N−1) ≤ N, and ι(N−1) ≠ N = last, so ι(N−1) ≤ N − 1; and for k < N − 1, ι(k) < ι(k+1) gives by downward induction ι(k) ≤ k. Hence ι(k) = k for all k, i.e. ι = castSucc. Consequently range ι = {j : j ≠ last}, the integrand is y ↦ h(y) := ω(py)(e_0, …, e_{N−1}) by step 1, and F̃ = {y : ρz_{castSucc i} ≤ y_{castSucc i} ≤ ρ(z_{castSucc i} + 1) for all i ∈ Fin N, and y_last = ρz_last}.
4. The isometric embedding. Define j : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N+1} by j(x)_{castSucc i} := x_i (i ∈ Fin N) and j(x)_last := ρz_last. Then |j(x) − j(x')|² = Σ_i (x_i − x'_i)² = |x − x'|², so j is an isometry, hence a closed embedding and a measurable embedding; and p(j(x)) = x by the defining formula of p. By the description of F̃ in step 3, j(G) ⊆ F̃; conversely, if y ∈ F̃ then x := py satisfies x_i = y_{castSucc i}, so x ∈ G, and y = j(x) because the coordinates castSucc i agree and y_last = ρz_last. Thus j(G) = F̃. In particular every x ∈ G equals p(j(x)) with j(x) ∈ F̃, which is the last claim of (b).
5. Change of variables. By Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, μHE[N].map j = μHE[N].restrict (range j); with MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map and the injectivity of j, (μHE[N].restrict G).map j = (μHE[N].map j).restrict (j(G)) = μHE[N].restrict (j(G) ∩ range j) = μHE[N].restrict (j(G)). Hence, by MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map (valid for every function), ∫_{F̃} h dHᴺ = ∫_{j(G)} h dHᴺ = ∫_G h∘j dHᴺ = ∫_G ω(p(j(x)))(e_0, …, e_{N−1}) dHᴺ(x) = ∫_G ω(x)(e_0, …, e_{N−1}) dHᴺ(x). ∎

Horizontal cells: a strictly increasing ι avoiding last is castSucc, and F̃ = j(G) for the isometric embedding j(x) = (x, ρz_last) with p∘j = id.

The triple R_{z,b} := (G_z, |b|, σξ₀), with constant multiplicity mult := fun _ => b.natAbs ≥ 1 and constant orientation σξ₀ (so (b.natAbs : ℝ)·σ = b), is an IMRep in ℝⁿ: G_z is closed, hence Borel, and ⊆ univ; it is countably n-rectifiable since G_z ⊆ ℝⁿ = range(id) with id 1-Lipschitz (countablyRectifiable_range and CountablyRectifiable.mono); constant maps are measurable and a.e. strongly measurable; for compact K, ∫⁻_{G_z ∩ K} |b| dHⁿ ≤ |b|·Hⁿ(G_z) = |b|ρⁿ < ∞ (G_z is a cube of side ρ, Hⁿ = Lebesgue measure); and the a.e. orientation condition holds by steps 2 and 3. By (IMC)(b) with U = ℝⁿ and E = ℝⁿ there are A_{z,b} ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝⁿ) and an IMRep with carrier G_z ∩ ℝⁿ = G_z, multiplicity |b| and orientation σξ₀ that represents A_{z,b}; so A_{z,b} is IM and A_{z,b}(ω) = ∫_{G_z} |b|·σ·ω(x)(e) dHⁿ(x) = b ∫_{G_z} ω(x)(e) dHⁿ(x). For b = 0 put A_{z,0} := 0, which is IM by step 1 and satisfies the same formula.
5. Sums. If A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝⁿ) are IM, then 0 − B is IM and A − (0 − B) is IM by (IMC)(c) (U = ℝⁿ open, 0 IM by step 1), and (A − (0 − B))(ω) = A(ω) + B(ω). By induction over the finite set s (Finset.induction), the current Y_s defined by Y_∅ := 0 and Y_{insert z s'} := A_{z,β_z} − (0 − Y_{s'}) (z ∉ s') is IM and satisfies Y_s(ω) = Σ_{z∈s} β_z ∫_{G_z} ω(x)(e) dHⁿ(x) for every ω.
6. By hypothesis X(ω) = Y_s(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝⁿ), so X = Y_s (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), and X is integer multiplicity. ∎

(c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B.
